**Telemetry scope — VM experience as observed by the hypervisor:** Libvirt/QEMU and host-network measurements. Ceph/RBD and physical-device telemetry measure other points; the views are complementary. Scope, units and graph guidance are in this panel’s help.

panels.description:
Scope: Instance and Project select UUID identities; names are labels and can repeat. Project name filter is an additional constraint. The hidden Hypervisor filter can be carried from another dashboard and is shown in the banner. Volume UUID limits storage panels; CPU, memory and network retain the instance selection. Reset scope clears these filters while keeping the time range and datasource.

Time: snapshot cards and current-observation tables are evaluated at the range end; historical graphs and retype outcomes use the selected range. Reachability and collection coverage follow hosting targets inferred from selected-instance inventory history. Migration can include previous and current hosts. Mining coverage uses the Hypervisor scope shown above.

Graphs: Top N limits each graph query independently to at most N series; multiple measurements can each return N lines. Selection stays fixed over the range. Max in range ranks the highest plotted sample; Mean in range ranks its average; Last observed ranks the latest available sample, which may precede the range end. Ranking and plotting use the same sampled interval; a peak between plotted points is not searched. 0 (All) uses the established large limit. These controls do not limit tables or the collection-coverage graph.

Legends: names and full UUIDs preserve identity. Colours distinguish instances or measurements, can repeat, and do not assign severity. Line styles distinguish paired measurements; stronger fill is not a health score. Legends start in descending Max order. Sorting a legend changes display order only. Scroll inside the legend, use the tooltip, or isolate a series. Last is the right-edge value and stays unavailable for ended series; Max is the highest plotted sample, not the largest individual I/O.

Tables: every matching row is returned. Scroll inside the table and click a column heading to sort. Names and field links open related dashboards; full identities remain available in Inspect → Data. A carried filter can narrow another view; Reset scope clears it.

Availability and units: a gap or empty table can mean missing observations, not healthy zero. Check reachability, resource freshness and collection coverage. Disk latency has no mean while no operations complete; explicit No I/O table values require usable counters. Throughput is bytes/s for disk and bits/s for network; memory is bytes. Grafana chooses IEC prefixes such as MiB and Gibit. Counter resets, migration and short windows can make rates spiky. VM-side I/O does not measure Ceph-wide volume totals, physical-device utilization or NIC/switch traffic.

panels.description:
Host-scheduler waiting summed across this VM’s vCPUs, in milliseconds per wall-clock second (ms/s), averaged over five minutes. 1000 ms/s is one vCPU-second of waiting per second; a multi-vCPU total can exceed 1000 ms/s. This is scheduling delay, not guest I/O wait, a CPU percentage or per-request latency.

Delay/steal is preferred for each vCPU; wait is a compatibility fallback and is not added to that vCPU’s delay. Rate-eligible counters must cover every allocated vCPU. Partial, missing or unhealthy observations leave a gap rather than understating the VM total.

panels.description:
Read, write and flush mean latency for each disk of running VMs with qualifying Libvirt/QEMU observations, in milliseconds over five minutes. Service time is divided by completed operations using the same disk, direction, window and sample counts. Each disk keeps its own identity; means are not averaged across disks.

No completed operations means there is no latency mean. Idle disks and missing, insufficient or unhealthy counter pairs leave gaps; neither means 0 ms. Read is solid, write dashed and flush dotted. Max is the highest plotted mean, not the slowest individual I/O. This is not direct Ceph/storage-backend latency, physical-media latency or application fsync latency.

Disk write throughput by disk (bytes/s with automatic IEC prefixes), top N volumes across instances.

Scope: VM virtual-disk counters observed through Libvirt/QEMU. These represent VM-side block activity seen at the hypervisor, not total backend operations, backend device utilization, or storage-pool performance. Caching, request merging, replication, snapshots, and other storage layers can make backend I/O differ.

Source: Libvirt/QEMU stats collected on the hypervisor by OIE.
Limitations: Host-side view of VM counters; guest OS reporting may differ. Counters can reset on VM reboot/migration; short rate windows can be spiky. Disk I/O counters are cumulative and typically visualized as rates; they may not include backend replication/cluster overhead.

panels.title: VM disk flush service-time rate (Top N)
Storage · disk attachments, source observations and retypes
Selected instances · VM-side disk I/O
panels.description:
One row per matching VM disk attachment at the range end, including local disks when Volume UUID is All. Read + write IOPS excludes flushes. Throughput is bytes/s; rates use $__rate_interval and require usable scrape/Libvirt observations throughout the window. Latency uses matching service-time/request counters and sample counts on the same attachment.

No I/O means both latency counters are present with zero completed-operation rate. Unavailable means missing, insufficient, stale or unhealthy telemetry. An empty table can mean no matching attachments or unavailable observations; check coverage.

Storage source is an RBD pool, non-RBD protocol or local/block source kind, not a physical-drive class or guaranteed Cinder volume type. Unclassified source means XML and runtime identity could not be mapped consistently; inspect Disk source observations for the device and inventory match. Known config drives, CD-ROMs and floppies belong to configured block-device inventory. VM-side values are not Ceph-wide volume totals, especially for multi-attach volumes. All matching rows are shown; scroll or sort the table.

panels.title: Selected instances · disk source observations
panels.description:
Configured storage disks/LUNs from Libvirt XML plus runtime block-stat devices that have no matching configured storage device. Rows match exporter target, instance UUID and device path. Observation distinguishes configured from runtime-only records; runtime-only can mean incomplete or changing metadata and does not prove a CD-ROM.

Storage source is the existing disk_type label: an RBD pool, non-RBD protocol or local/block source kind, not a physical-drive class or guaranteed Cinder volume type. Unclassified source means the runtime device could not be mapped to a recognised source. Backing volume / path is an observed identity and may be a local path. No labels are invented, and no physical allocation, backend free space, runtime usage or authoritative Cinder state is inferred. Known config drives, CD-ROMs and floppies are inventory-only. All matching rows are shown; scroll or sort the table.

panels.description:
One row per recently confirmed attached-RBD volume retype operation observed through Libvirt/QEMU. Instance, disk, source image/pool and destination image/pool identify the operation, so multiple retypes on one hypervisor or instance remain separate. Rows use OIE’s bounded active-observation window; a missing fresh progress observation does not turn retained identity into measured progress.

Logical Progress is cur/end work position, not transferred bytes or an ETA. Libvirt Observation shows whether progress polling was usable. Observed Elapsed is time since OIE first saw the operation; missing optional values remain Unavailable or a dash. Copying / finalizing, Ready / awaiting pivot and Ready stalled describe OIE’s observed stages; Ready stalled means at least ten minutes ready. Cinder remains authoritative for control-plane state and timestamps.

Monitoring must be enabled. Empty results can mean no matching operations, disabled monitoring or missing observations; check collection coverage and the Cluster retype overview. Volume UUID matches the source RBD image. All matching operations are shown; scroll or sort the table.

panels.title: Active attached-volume retypes

panels.description:
Captured terminal observations for attached-RBD volume retypes within the selected time range. Instance, disk, source image/pool and destination image/pool identify each operation, so multiple retypes on one hypervisor or instance remain separate. Completed (code 2) means the destination became live; Unsuccessful / Cancelled (code 3) means the original source stayed live; Outcome Unknown (code 4) means OIE could not match the final backing image. These are observations, not authoritative Cinder outcomes.

Terminal states have a one-minute terminal grace; Prometheus history preserves captured samples. This table reconstructs that history for the selected range. Terminal Observed is when OIE first confirmed the Libvirt mirror gone, normally within the active poll cadence, not an authoritative Cinder completion timestamp. Missing optional timestamps remain a dash.

Monitoring must have been enabled to capture an operation. Empty results can mean no captured matching outcomes, disabled monitoring or missing observations; check collection coverage and the Cluster retype overview. Volume UUID matches the source RBD image. All matching captured operations are shown; scroll or sort the table.

Inbound destination ports from Linux kernel conntrack for each fixed IP and address family. Top N is applied independently to the unique and new queries, so the panel can return up to 2N lines. These describe observed connection breadth, not proof of scanning or abuse. Missing or unhealthy conntrack observations leave a gap.

Threat observations · active-flow and contact matches

panels.description:
Sum of per-list, per-direction active-flow match counts attributed to each instance. This is a sum of matches, not a distinct-flow count: the same kernel conntrack entry can contribute through multiple configured lists and/or directions. Available list sources are unioned before aggregation, so a disabled or unavailable list does not suppress the other sources.

Source: Linux kernel conntrack state collected by OIE and evaluated against configured threat-feed snapshots.
Limitations: Feed overlap, coverage, freshness, host visibility, and current fixed-IP attribution bound interpretation; list matches are evidence, not proof.

panels.title: VM threat-list active-flow matches (Top N)

panels.description:
Five-minute per-second rate summed across available per-list, per-direction threat-contact counters for each instance. This is a sum of contact matches, not a distinct-contact rate: the same kernel conntrack event can contribute through multiple configured lists and/or directions. Available list sources are unioned before aggregation, so a disabled or unavailable list does not suppress the other sources.

Source: Linux kernel conntrack state collected by OIE and evaluated against configured threat-feed snapshots.
Limitations: Feed overlap, coverage, freshness, scrape gaps, counter resets, host visibility, and current fixed-IP attribution bound interpretation; list matches are evidence, not proof.

list.label: Hypervisor
list.name: gvar_oie_hypervisor
list.description: Configured OIE scrape targets, including empty and unreachable hypervisors. Instance presence does not determine host visibility.

list.label: Project
list.name: gvar_oie_project_uuid
list.description: Project name and full UUID. Filtering and links use the UUID, so duplicate names remain distinct.

list.label: Project name filter
list.name: gvar_oie_project_name
list.description: Additional name constraint on the selected Project UUIDs. Duplicate names can match more than one UUID. Keep All unless a name filter is needed; Reset scope clears carried filters.

list.label: Instance
list.name: gvar_oie_instance_uuid
list.description: Select All, several instances, or one instance. Names are displayed with full UUIDs; queries and links use UUID identity.

list.name: gvar_oie_volume_uuid
list.label: Volume UUID (disk panels)
list.description: Limits matching storage panels to source/backing volume identities. All also includes local disks. CPU, memory and network keep the selected instance scope. Retype tables match the source RBD image, not the destination.

list.label: Top N / query
list.name: gvar_oie_top_n
list.description: Maximum matching series per graph query, not a guaranteed number of lines or visible legend rows. Multiple queries can each return N series. 0 (All) uses the existing large graph limit. Tables are not limited.

list.label: Select top series by
list.name: gvar_oie_rank_by
list.query: Last observed : last_over_time,Max in range : max_over_time,Mean in range : avg_over_time
list.description: Max in range (default) selects the highest plotted values in the selected time window. Mean in range uses their average. Last observed uses the last available sample, which may predate the range end; earlier peaks can be excluded. Saved URL selections remain active. Legend column sorting changes display order only. Full graph, legend and table guidance is in the Scope, time and dashboard help panel.

title: OpenStack Instance Exporter — Instance Overview
description: OIE measurements, resource state and investigation views. Requires exporter scraping only; notification rules are optional. Missing data is not health.
